The [QR Code Generator](/qr-code-generator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Create and download a QR code for a link, text or contact detail. Open it and start straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Turn a URL or plain text into a crisp QR code, choose its size and error correction, then download it as a PNG. Generation happens locally in your browser with no account and no tracking pixel. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers. Related Image & Media tools include [Image Resizer](/image-resizer), [Aspect Ratio Calculator](/aspect-ratio-calculator) and [Color Code Converter](/color-code-converter).

## How to use the QR Code Generator

Open the [QR Code Generator](/qr-code-generator) and start straight away — there is no form to fill in first. The result updates as you work, so you can try different settings and see the change straight away.

1. Check the result — it updates instantly as you type.
2. Use Reset to start over with the default values.

## Formula

The QR specification encodes your text as modules. Higher error correction allows more damage to be recovered but creates a denser code.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [QR Code Generator](/qr-code-generator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic. If the figures look wrong, check your inputs first — a misplaced decimal point is the usual culprit.

## Trying it out

The fastest way to see what the [QR Code Generator](/qr-code-generator) does is to open it and enter values you already know the answer for. Change one input at a time and watch how the result responds — that tells you more than any description. Everything runs in your browser, so you can experiment freely: nothing is saved, sent or tracked.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Always scan the finished code before printing it.
- Keep a clear quiet zone around the code.
- Higher error correction is useful when placing a small logo over the code.

Keep these in mind and the figures will be as useful as the numbers you put in.

## Frequently asked questions

### Do QR codes expire?

A static QR code containing your text does not expire. A linked website can still go offline. Try it with your own numbers in the [QR Code Generator](/qr-code-generator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Is the content sent to a server?

No. The QR image is generated in your browser. Try it with your own numbers in the [QR Code Generator](/qr-code-generator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the QR Code Generator use?

The QR specification encodes your text as modules. Higher error correction allows more damage to be recovered but creates a denser code. You can see it in action in the [QR Code Generator](/qr-code-generator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

Yes. The QR Code Generator is free to use as often as you like, with no sign-up. There is no limit on how often you use it, nothing to install, and no account to create — open the [QR Code Generator](/qr-code-generator) and start straight away.
